entry.title: A single malloc took 7 milliseconds. So I deleted the slow path.
entry.summary:
Every allocator benchmark leads with the median. malloc does 15M ops/sec, the typical call is 15 ns, ship it. The median never paged me at 3 a.m. The tail did. Same allocator, same workload, but measuring the worst single call instead of the typical one: Median: ~16 ns
Worst case: 6,950,000 ns — almost 7 milliseconds. One malloc, occasionally, taking seven milliseconds. If you're rendering a frame in 16 ms or quoting a price in a market, that call just ate your entire budget — and the average looked fantastic the whole time. General allocators are fast on average because they have a slow path. Thread caches, coalescing, tree walks, OS fallback. Most calls dodge it. The ones that don't are your tail. So I built PMAD, and made the opposite bet: delete the slow path entirely. One mmap at sta…
